name: Hatchobori
tagline: Tokyo in 2 minutes and Otemachi in 9 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000.
summary: The station is in Chuo City, where JR East and Tokyo Metro run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 9 minutes to Otemachi, 23 minutes to Shinjuku, 27 minutes to Shibuya and 17 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. The station stands 2.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 3.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 2.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from -0.6 m to 3.2 m, a difference of 3.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 5 to 10 m. For storm surge, 2 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 9 clinics and 9 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is いしせ脳神経外科クリニック, about 6 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 聖路加国際病院, about 14 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: JR Keiyo Line and Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 1 line and Tokyo Metro runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line runs at 163% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 三ノ輪→入谷, which this station is not on. JR Keiyo Line runs at 123%. Its busiest stretch is 葛西臨海公園→新木場, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000 and 2LDK ¥310,000 to ¥320,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the lowest in the 23 wards. What holds the figure down: a large projected flood depth. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Hatchobori, but Kyobashi is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Hatchobori. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Hatchobori. One-room rents run about ¥22,000 higher.

neighbours.lead: Kayabacho is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Hatchobori is ahead on how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Hatchobori. It reaches Otemachi 5 minutes sooner than Hatchobori.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want a park close by
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線 viaduct runs a short walk from the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
新大橋通り (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 8 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 4 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the lowest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are some of the most heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
